transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tom (Acme Head of Security), Maria (IT Ops), Evan (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick security and compliance review focused on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege model. Discussed audit logs, KMS integration, data residency concerns for PHI-ish data in EMEA, and next steps for pilot.

Topics:
- SAML SSO flow and IdP metadata
- SCIM provisioning and group sync cadence
- RBAC roles, least-privilege defaults, separation of duties
- Audit logs retention and export options
- Encryption at rest and KMS/HSM integration
- SOC2/ISO evidence and auditor contacts

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we're gonna run through the SSO and RBAC stuff, quick intros?
[00:07] Tom: yeah hi Tom Reynolds, head of security at Acme Health, thanks for making time.
[00:11] Maria: Maria - IT ops, i'll be doing the provisioning and network bits.
[00:14] Alex: great, priya do you wanna kick off the SSO overview?
[00:17] Priya: sure, yep. so Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for enterprise SSO, we also do SCIM for automated user and group provisioning, typical flow is you upload the SP metadata to your IdP, we return an ACS URL and entity ID, you configure the claim mappings.
[00:34] Priya: we normally recommend mapping email to the 'userName' and include groups as an array, so group-based RBAC works. sometimes the IdP calls it memberOf or groups, so that mapping is where we see small issues.
[00:48] Maria: ok question - can we restrict SCIM so only a subset of groups sync into prod? we don't want contractor accounts.
[00:54] Priya: yes you can - on Redwood side we support scoping by group filters and an allowlist; you can configure SCIM to only provision groups that match a prefix, e g 'acme-prod-*'. also you can set provisioning to manual approval.
[01:07] Tom: how about SCIM patch latency? we need near real-time for offboarding, ideally <60s.
[01:13] Priya: typical delta is a few seconds to a minute depending on IdP, we've seen Okta push immediate patches; worst case with scheduled syncs it's a couple minutes. not perfect but within many teams' SLA.
[01:26] Evan: and deprovisioning - does it remove tokens/sessions immediately? we need sessions terminated on offboard.
[01:32] Priya: good callout. we revoke long-lived API keys on SCIM delete events and invalidate active sessions by marking user disabled; session termination depends on token TTL but we also support force sign-out via the admin API. we'll include the API call samples.
[01:46] Alex: switching to RBAC - priya you had a sample role map?
[01:50] Priya: yep, so our recommended least-privilege model is: 'Org Admin' for billing and account-level settings, 'Security Admin' for audit log access and SSO config, 'Model Ops' for deployment/rollout actions, and 'Viewer' for read-only dashboards. each role can be assigned to groups from SCIM.
[02:09] Tom: does Security Admin have the ability to export full logs? we want to limit that to a small group.
[02:16] Priya: yes you can gate log export behind a specific permission. by default only 'Security Admin' and 'Org Admin' get export privileges; you can create a custom role if you want separation.
[02:27] Tom: sounds good, we need separation of duties - auditors shouldn't be able to change SSO config.
[02:32] Priya: totally, that's a common pattern. our role matrix supports fine-grained permissions on SAML config, SCIM, audit log access, API key rotation, etc. we'll send the role matrix spreadsheet.
[02:44] Maria: question about SAML assertions: do you require signed assertions?
[02:48] Priya: we support both signed assertions and signed requests; we recommend signed assertions for additional security. we can also validate audience and recipient fields.
[02:58] Alex: talking encryption - at rest we use AES-256 and customer keys can be managed via KMS - priya can you explain KMS integrations?
[03:06] Priya: sure, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via common KMS vendors, like AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM-backed providers for on-prem. you can opt into CMEK for all model artifacts and persisted data. note: there is additional operational complexity for key rotation and backups.
[03:22] Tom: for PHI data we need HSM-backed keys and no key material leaving our KMS. is that possible?
[03:28] Priya: yes, with our Private deployment option you can integrate your HSM and manage keys on-prem; for Hosted we can support KMS so that key material never leaves the customer's control but you need to review the key wrapping details. we'll follow up with the KMS integration doc.
[03:43] Evan: does Redwood produce a key-use audit for each decrypt? we need evidence for auditors.
[03:48] Priya: we log key-use events and can include that in exports; retention is configurable, default 90 days but can be extended on enterprise plans.
[03:58] Tom: audit logs retention - we prefer 1 year, maybe longer for compliance. what's typical?
[04:03] Priya: default is 90 days for hosted, enterprise can bump to 1 year or more, and we can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export for archival.
[04:14] Alex: on data residency - Acme has EU data residency requirements for certain datasets, right tom?
[04:19] Tom: yes, all PHI-related inference calls must remain in EU region and logs retained in EU.
[04:24] Priya: Redwood can pin model serving to specific regions and we can set up dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 or a private deployment in your VPC; logs can be stored in EU-only buckets. there's some lead time for dedicated capacity provisioning.
[04:38] Maria: any network controls - can we lock down egress to specific IPs?
[04:42] Priya: yes if you're on Dedicated or Private, we provide static IP ranges and can set up VPC peering; for Hosted we have IP ranges per region.
[04:52] Alex: Tom raised SOC2/ISO earlier - we have a SOC2 Type II report, and ISO certificate; we can provide the auditor package and control mappings.
[04:59] Tom: do you have any customer attestations for healthcare?
[05:02] Alex: we do some healthcare customers on Dedicated/Private; we'll share redacted contracts and the security whitepaper.
[05:08] Tom: perfect.
[05:12] Maria: quick clarifying - SCIM group sync frequency, can we set to immediate?
[05:16] Priya: immediate if your IdP pushes events (Okta has push hooks); otherwise we poll every minute by default. you can reduce to 30s in Dedicated but that's an ops call.
[05:27] Evan: about session TTLs - can we set short-living tokens for interactive users but allow service accounts longer TTLs?
[05:34] Priya: yep that's supported; service account keys are long-lived but auditable, and interactive sessions can have short TTL and refresh tokens disabled for strict environments.
[05:45] Tom: what about SAML metadata rotation and certificate expiry? we need automation.
[05:49] Priya: we support metadata endpoints and auto-refresh; cert expiry alerts go to the admin emails and via the console. you can also upload new certs programmatically.
[05:58] Alex: any blockers from anyone - network, procurement, legal?
[06:02] Tom: procurement will want the DPA and security annex, legal needs to review KMS details.
[06:07] Alex: we'll attach the DPA and security annex, and I'll introduce our legal/security contact to Tom's team.
[06:14] Priya: action wise i'll drop the RBAC role matrix and API examples for force sign-out and token revocation.
[06:21] Maria: i'll compile the list of admin IDs and groups to sync.
[06:25] Tom: and i'll send over the auditor contact and regulatory scope.
[06:29] Alex: great, to recap next steps - Alex send SAML/SCIM metadata + DPA, Priya send RBAC and KMS integration doc, customer to schedule pilot and share admin list.
[06:40] Tom: thanks, this was useful.
[06:43] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and update the CRM. bye.
